I've opened PR #26535 implementing this feature with a minimal, permission-gated approach:

- Adds an optional `model` parameter to the task tool (`provider/model` format)
- `model_override` permission denied by default -- users opt in via config (e.g. `"model_override": { "anthropic/*": "allow" }`)
- Validates `provider/model` format with clear error messages
- Model priority: `params.model` -> `agent.model` -> parent session model

This is similar to #18528 but uses Effect Schema instead of zod and inlines the parsing to avoid importing the heavy Provider module. Compared to #11217 (UI-driven `@agent:provider/model`) and #11377 (tier abstraction), this takes the simplest direct approach with the security gate from the original issue.

@thdxr as I mentioned in the steps to reproduce, the model itself is executing the kill command. In my case, DeepSeek V4 Pro decided to run Stop-Process in PowerShell to kill a stale Node server.

However, I want to add that this has now happened twice in v1.14.41. At first, I thought it was just a corrupted session from my previous setup, so I did a completely clean/hard uninstall of OpenCode (wiping the app, all configs, everything).

After the clean install, it happened again on v1.14.41, this time while using a Kimi model. This second time, it wasn't even a kill process (I can't remember exactly what command it ran because the terminal instantly went completely crazy).

IMHO, this suggests it's not just tied to Stop-Process, but rather any command execution/hand-off by the model can potentially interrupt the TUI lifecycle and leave the terminal flooded.

@manascb1344 — Looked into this pretty deeply. Short answer: not with the current plugin API — Conclave touches too many internals that plugins can't reach yet.

The plugin system has hooks for intercepting messages, modifying params, registering tools, transforming system prompts, etc. But what Conclave actually does is hijack the entire response generation flow before the normal pipeline runs. In session/processor.ts there's ~230 lines that run a multi-turn debate, pick a winner, swap the model, handle concurrent sub-team implementation with fallbacks, and route CLI winners to agent-mode subprocesses. None of that maps to existing hooks.
The main gaps:

- No pre-processing hook that can replace the normal LLM call. Conclave needs to run 2–4 models debating before the "real" response ever happens. chat.message lets you see incoming messages but can't swap out the reply mechanism.

- No way to stream multiple model outputs simultaneously to the TUI. The debate shows live reasoning from each participant — the current streaming is single-model.

- No hook on the session status types. Conclave adds team.debate and team.breaking statuses. Plugins don't have a way to extend that enum.

- No custom config schema registration. Conclave adds a team section to the config. The config hook gives you read-only access to what already exists, not a way to add new sections.

That said, I think the right move isn't asking for a plugin API that does all of this — that'd be a monster. The right move is probably one targeted hook: something like chat.process that lets a plugin say "I'll handle this message, don't run the normal pipeline." If that existed, most of the debate engine could live in a plugin and just return the chosen model + the debate transcript back to the normal flow. The streaming part would still be rough but doable with the TUI slot system.
